words.translation: How do you get to work?

contrasts.title: Location, destination, origin
contrasts.tip: Think: place · to a place · from a place. The verb and preposition may also affect the case.

contrasts.title: Who does what?
contrasts.tip: The verb helps determine the case: helfen takes dative, while sehen takes accusative.

contrasts.title: Ask about amount or choice

items.meaning: How much time do you have?
How many books do you have?

contrasts.tip: Wie viele is used with countable plural nouns. Welcher changes form to match the noun.

patterns.label: Past · Perfekt
patterns.structure: Question word + helper + subject + rest + participle

patterns.label: Modal verb
patterns.structure: Question word + modal + subject + rest + infinitive
patterns.translation: When do you have to leave?

practice.prompt: Ask where someone lives. Answer: They live in Hamburg.
practice.question: Wo wohnst du?
practice.tip: Wo asks for a location. The answer gives the place.

practice.prompt: Ask where someone is going. Answer: To the train station.
practice.question: Wohin gehst du?
practice.answerTranslation: I’m going to the train station.
practice.tip: Wohin asks for a destination. Zum is zu + dem.

practice.prompt: Ask when the appointment starts. Answer: At 10 o’clock.
practice.question: Wann beginnt der Termin?
practice.tip: The verb beginnt follows the first question element Wann.

practice.prompt: Ask why someone is learning German. Answer with a reason.
practice.question: Warum lernst du Deutsch?
practice.answer: Weil ich in Deutschland arbeiten möchte.
practice.answerTranslation: Because I would like to work in Germany.
practice.tip: After weil, the conjugated verb moves to the end: arbeiten möchte.

practice.prompt: Ask what someone did yesterday. Answer: I cooked soup.
practice.question: Was hast du gestern gemacht?
practice.answer: Ich habe gestern eine Suppe gekocht.
practice.tip: In the question, hast is in position two and gemacht goes at the end.

practice.prompt: Ask which bus someone is taking. Answer: The number 5 bus.
practice.question: Welchen Bus nimmst du?
practice.answer: Ich nehme den Bus Nummer fünf.
practice.tip: Welchen matches Bus in the accusative because it is the object of nehmen.

practice.prompt: Ask how someone gets to work. Answer: By bicycle.
practice.question: Wie kommst du zur Arbeit?
practice.questionTranslation: How do you get to work?
practice.answer: Ich fahre mit dem Fahrrad zur Arbeit.
practice.answerTranslation: I go to work by bicycle.
practice.tip: Wie asks about the way or method. Mit takes the dative: mit dem Fahrrad.

practice.prompt: Ask how long the German course lasts. Answer: Six months.
practice.question: Wie lange dauert der Deutschkurs?
practice.questionTranslation: How long does the German course last?
practice.answerTranslation: The German course lasts six months.
practice.tip: Wie lange asks about duration. The verb dauern describes how long something lasts.

practice.prompt: Ask how often someone practises German. Answer: Every day.
practice.question: Wie oft übst du Deutsch?
practice.questionTranslation: How often do you practise German?
practice.tip: Wie oft asks about frequency. Jeden Tag is a common answer.

practice.prompt: Ask whom someone is calling. Answer: Her colleague.
practice.question: Wen rufst du an?
practice.tip: Anrufen is separable: the prefix an goes to the end. Wen asks for the accusative object.

practice.prompt: Ask whom someone is helping. Answer: Their neighbour.
practice.question: Wem hilfst du?
practice.tip: Helfen takes the dative, so ask Wem? and answer meinem Nachbarn.

practice.prompt: Ask where someone came from yesterday. Answer: From Munich.
practice.question: Woher bist du gestern gekommen?
practice.questionTranslation: Where did you come from yesterday?
practice.answer: Ich bin gestern aus München gekommen.
practice.tip: Woher asks about origin. In Perfekt, bist is in position two and gekommen goes at the end.

practice.prompt: Ask how many siblings someone has. Answer: Two.
practice.question: Wie viele Geschwister hast du?
practice.questionTranslation: How many siblings do you have?
practice.tip: Wie viele is used with a countable plural noun: die Geschwister.

practice.prompt: Ask which language someone speaks at home. Answer: Turkish.
practice.question: Welche Sprache sprichst du zu Hause?
practice.questionTranslation: Which language do you speak at home?
practice.tip: Welche matches the feminine noun Sprache. A time or place phrase can come first in the answer; the verb stays second.

practice.prompt: Ask whose bag this is. Answer: It belongs to Anna.
practice.question: Wessen Tasche ist das?
practice.tip: Wessen asks about possession. It is useful to recognize, though everyday speakers may also ask Wem gehört die Tasche?

practice.prompt: Ask what time the train leaves. Answer: At 8:15.
practice.question: Wann fährt der Zug ab?
practice.answer: Der Zug fährt um acht Uhr fünfzehn ab.
practice.tip: Abfahren is separable: the prefix ab goes at the end of the main clause.

practice.prompt: Ask what someone has to bring to the appointment. Answer: Their passport.
practice.question: Was musst du zum Termin mitbringen?
practice.questionTranslation: What do you have to bring to the appointment?
practice.answerTranslation: I have to bring my passport.
practice.tip: With a modal, musst is in position two and mitbringen stays as an infinitive at the end.
